member.name: T:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbConnectionFactory
member.summary:
Opens DuckDB connections. DuckDB runs in-process and has no connection pool; instead, a database instance lives as long as at least one connection to it is open, and DuckDB.NET shares one instance between connections opened with the same data source. This factory therefore opens one root connection on first use and keeps it open until it is disposed. Every connection it hands out shares the root's database instance (in-memory connections are s of the root; file connections are opened with the same data source):
:memory: (or an empty data source): an in-memory database private to this factory. All repositories sharing the factory see the same data; raw connections opened with the same connection string do not (each would get its own empty database). The database is released when the factory is disposed.
:memory:?cache=shared: the process-wide shared in-memory database. Raw connections with the same string share it; it lives while any connection to it (including this factory's root) is open.
A file path: the database file. The root connection keeps the database open (and DuckDB's file lock held: a read-write file can be opened by one process at a time) until the factory is disposed, which avoids re-opening and checkpointing the file for every operation.
Concurrency: DuckDB uses optimistic multi-version concurrency control. Concurrent transactions do not block each other; a transaction that updates or deletes a row changed by another concurrent transaction fails with a "Conflict on update" error (a ) instead of waiting, so callers that update the same rows from several threads should retry such failures. Thread safety: safe for concurrent use.

member.name: T:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbDataTypeConverter
member.summary: DuckDB value conversion. DuckDB.NET binds and reads most CLR types natively (including unsigned integers, GUIDs as UUID, DateOnly/TimeOnly, TimeSpan as INTERVAL and DateTimeOffset as TIMESTAMPTZ). This converter covers what the driver returns in other shapes: BLOB columns are read as a (copied to a byte array), HUGEINT/UHUGEINT values (for example SUM over integer columns) are read as and narrowed to the target numeric type, and values are written with unspecified kind for TIMESTAMP columns. Thread safety: stateless; safe for concurrent use.

member.name: T:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbDialect
member.summary: DuckDB dialect (DuckDB 1.1+, as bundled with DuckDB.NET.Data.Full). Tables are resolved in current_database() and current_schema() unless the name is schema-qualified. Notable differences from PostgreSQL, which DuckDB's SQL otherwise follows: auto-increment keys use a sequence per column (DEFAULT nextval(...), because DuckDB has no identity columns), savepoints are not supported ( is false), integer division uses //, and the migration lock is a row in (DuckDB has no advisory locks; see ). Thread safety: immutable; safe to share.

member.name: P:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbDialect.SupportsTransactionalDdl
member.remarks: Reported as false although DuckDB can roll back DDL: DuckDB cannot create an index in a transaction that has already changed rows of the table (for example by adding a column with a default) and cannot drop a column in the transaction that dropped its index, which schema synchronization and typical migrations need. Durable therefore applies migrations and schema changes statement by statement (each commits on its own), as on MySQL; a failed migration may leave its earlier statements applied.

member.remarks: DuckDB ignores declared string lengths, so strings are always VARCHAR (MaxLength is not enforced by the database). Unsigned integers use DuckDB's native unsigned types, (for example from a value converter) maps to HUGEINT, and JSON columns use the JSON type.

member.name: M:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbDialect.AppendCreateTable(Durable.Sql.SqlStatementBuilder,Durable.EntityMetadata)
member.remarks: Each auto-increment column gets a sequence named {table}_{column}_seq (in the table's schema), and the column defaults to nextval of it. DuckDB does not drop a sequence with the table that uses it, so the statement first drops a sequence of that name left behind by an earlier, dropped table and recreates it: a recreated table numbers its rows from 1 again, as on the other databases. The engine emits this statement only for tables that do not exist; when the table does exist, DuckDB refuses to drop the sequence it depends on and the statement fails instead of being a no-op.

member.name: M:Durable.DuckDb.DuckDbDialect.AcquireMigrationLockSql(System.String,System.Int32)
member.remarks: DuckDB has no advisory or session locks. The lock is a row in (created on first use): the statement inserts the row and yields 1, or yields no row when another session holds the lock. Concurrent attempts that DuckDB reports as write-write conflicts or key violations count as "not acquired" (). A DuckDB file is opened read-write by one process at a time, so rows left by another process (one that exited without releasing) are stale and removed first. waitSeconds is not used: the migrator polls.
